category_title: Bored students who engage in off-task behaviors
minimal_context: An 8th grade student is asked to solve algebra problems dictated from a course book.
dialogue:
TUTOR: Please open your course books. I am going to dictate the algebra problems for you to solve.

STUDENT: When the teacher lectures in a plain way, I cannot solve the problems in that course.

TUTOR: Just keep reading from the book and write down what I say.

STUDENT: Some of our teachers lecture so plain, that is, there is no visuality or discussion and interpretation, we just read from our course books, thus the classes are boring and I don’t like paying attention to the course.

TUTOR: It has been 20 minutes, you need to focus only on the course.

STUDENT: They come, they tell and tell and tell and leave, they only dictate even in algebra. We feel sleepy, one of our friends felt asleep during the course.

options.A: Make the algebra course amusing, make an effort to keep the student's attention alive, and encourage the student to participate in the lesson.
options.B: Ignore the student's complaints about the algebra course and continue dictating the problems from the book (where safe to do so).
options.C: Ask the student to either rewrite the dictated algebra problem as an equation or write down the specific variables they are solving for.
options.D: Use two boards and solve the algebra problem alongside the student. Identify the mistake, show it to the student, wipe the board clean, and try again.
